lessons.claim: A check with no satisfiable solution when real physical values are put in is a check that is wrong. Setting the neglect-of-inertia condition as tau_p/dt <= 1e-2 left trap-2d-5um with no dt at all satisfying 100*tau_p <= dt <= 0.01*tau_k. The cause is that BD has no inertia (HOOMD's Brownian has no mass in the equation) -- tau_p is a model-validity condition rather than a numerical one, so it had to be compared against tau_dyn. That golden_trap was 0.38 percent accurate at tau_p/dt=4000 is the evidence
